start:
1. Read collection_info, list_decks and list_notetypes. Work only in the currently open profile.
2. Use IDs returned by tools; 64-bit protobuf IDs may be strings, tool inputs require integers. Note IDs and card IDs differ.
3. Search using Anki browser syntax. Read all result pages before claiming a complete set.
4. Inspect get_notetype before any note writes. Names may be localized or customized. Fields are HTML strings; preserve omitted fields.
5. Use usage_guide for image_occlusion, notetypes, media or learning. Tool schemas define exact input types; native_schema exposes native Anki options.
6. Ask the user to clarify ambiguous target content. Confirm scope before destructive edits; confirm=true is a tool argument, not evidence of user intent. Preserve medical sources provided by the user and never invent citations.
7. A tool error may have partial effects. Inspect the state before retrying. Undo applies to supported collection changes, not all media/file operations.
8. Use preview_notes for native HTML previews before adding notes. Use audit_notes(query,required_fields=[actual source field name]) to locate technical gaps; it does not verify medical facts or source reliability.
image_occlusion:
Native Image Occlusion workflow:
1. Call list_notetypes. A displayed name like Bildverdeckung, Image Occlusion or Ankiphil - iOcclusion is not proof of a format. native_image_occlusion=true / original_stock_kind=6 identifies the native type; use get_notetype to inspect it.
2. Upload the supplied diagram with store_media(filename, data_base64), and use the ACTUAL returned filename. Or choose existing collection media with list_media.
3. Call get_image(filename) so a vision-capable client can see the actual image. read_media returns bytes for transfer, not an image presentation. If the client cannot see images, request a vision tool or explicit coordinates; do not guess masks or anatomical labels.
4. Rectangles are normalized to the whole image: left=x/image_width, top=y/image_height, width=mask_width/image_width, height=mask_height/image_height. Every rectangle must fit inside 0..1. Mask the intended label, not unrelated anatomy.
5. Call create_image_occlusion with deck_id, filename, optional native notetype_id, rectangles, header, back_extra and tags. Example rectangles: [{"ordinal":1,"left":0.10,"top":0.20,"width":0.25,"height":0.08},{"ordinal":2,"left":0.55,"top":0.35,"width":0.20,"height":0.08}]. This creates two cards; equal ordinals group multiple rectangles on ONE card. Ordinals start at 1.
6. Verify get_image_occlusion and get_cards(render=true), and review anatomical accuracy with the user. The image tool does not replace medical judgement.
7. update_image_occlusion edits existing native masks. Removed masks can leave empty cards preserving history; inspect empty_cards before explicit delete_cards.
8. Native advanced shapes can be passed via occlusions markup, mutually exclusive with rectangles. Only use syntax validated from existing native notes or Anki documentation; do not invent ellipse/polygon markup.
9. A third-party type with original_stock_kind != 6 is not automatically supported by create_image_occlusion. Inspect its fields and templates. Ordinary fields/media can be updated, but extension-specific mask generators and UI editors are not exposed automatically. For a new native layout, clone_notetype from a native occlusion type and retain its native fields and template logic.
notetypes:
You can create and manage custom note types. 1. list_notetypes includes real localized field names and native kind. get_notetype returns all fields, templates, CSS and originalStockKind. Do not assume that Einfach, Basic, Ankiphil or Image Q/A share a schema. 2. create_notetype creates a standard or cloze type. Example: {"name":"Medizin - Quellenkarten","fields":["Frage","Antwort","Quelle"],"templates":[{"name":"Vorwärts","qfmt":"{{Frage}}","afmt":"{{FrontSide}}
{{Antwort}}
{{Quelle}}"},{"name":"Rückwärts","qfmt":"{{Antwort}}","afmt":"{{FrontSide}}
{{Frage}}
{{Quelle}}"}],"css":".card {font-family:Arial;font-size:22px;text-align:left}","cloze":false}. Each qualifying template generates a card per note. 3. add_notes uses the NEW returned notetype ID and exact field names. HTML images use , audio/video uses [sound:returned-filename]. 4. For cloze=true, use a cloze filter in the template (e.g. {{cloze:Text}}) and fields containing {{c1::...}}. Use the returned field names, which may be translated. 5. Prefer clone_notetype to preserve a complex existing type. Clone the native occlusion type to customize its presentation without losing native mask fields. create_notetype(cloze=true) alone does NOT create a native occlusion type. 6. update_notetype changes name/CSS/fields/templates; read the full native record first, preserve ord values of existing fields/templates, supply complete ordered arrays for flds/tmpls. Template/field removals can delete cards/data and require confirm=true. 7. change_notetype converts existing notes. field_map and template_map are TARGET index -> SOURCE index, -1 means blank/new. Preview mappings carefully, preserve sources and history. This operation can remove cards. 8. Existing third-party templates can be inspected and cloned. Their dependent JavaScript, CSS/media assets or add-on-specific editing features may still require the original add-on. 9. Before add_notes, preview_notes accepts the same note entries and returns native HTML/CSS without saving. Conditional standard templates are all previewed; actual card generation can omit empty ones.
learning:
Use learning_overview(query) for a study dashboard and learning_statistics(query,days) for native graphs. Review logs are in review_history; card_statistics adds native FSRS data. Due values have queue-dependent units: use native stats and scheduler_day.
Inspect get_deck_options and native_schema(deck_config/deck_limits). set_deck_options clones a preset by default; shared=true changes all decks assigned to it. global_fsrs is collection-wide. fsrs_parameters computes/evaluates but does not apply settings automatically.
Search card IDs before schedule_cards; tags belong to notes, suspension/flags to cards. Never submit answer_card or reset learning merely to improve metrics. Actual answers require explicit user intent and change scheduling/history.
Use audit_notes on the target topic, with required_fields naming the actual source/answer fields. Empty optional fields are listed but not flagged as missing required data. Reports cover only each scanned page; follow next_offset.
media:
store_media accepts base64 bytes and returns an Anki collision-safe filename. Always use that returned filename in note HTML or sound references. get_image emits an actual MCP image block (up to 4 MiB PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP); requires a vision-capable client. read_media streams base64 chunks for binary transfer. list_media searches existing filenames.
No media-generation, OCR or audio-recording tool is built in; use client tools for those, then upload bytes. SVG/PDF needs client-side conversion for image viewing. The API accepts only plain filenames in the collection media folder.
Media operations have no collection Undo. trash_media uses Ankis media trash and restore_media_trash restores it. check_media can normalize filenames. ChatGPT tunnel size/time limits may be lower than the local tool limits.
quality:
Use preview_notes with the same notes array as add_notes, before saving generated cards. It renders native question/answer HTML and CSS without adding records. Duplicate first fields are warnings. It previews all standard templates, including conditional ones that may be omitted by actual card generation. Cloze ordinals are read by Anki. This is Ankis card-layout renderer: dynamic special fields such as Deck may show placeholders; deck_name gives the selected target deck. Rendering does not imply medical correctness.
Use audit_notes(query,required_fields=[exact localized fields],limit,offset) for existing notes. It lists empty optional fields, flags empty or missing REQUIRED fields, and checks local img/audio/video references and missing cloze markup. For source completeness, explicitly pass the real source field name from list_notetypes/get_notetype. A source field being populated does not prove its source exists or supports the fact. No network requests are made for remote URLs. Follow next_offset and report the scanned scope; do not present one page as a complete audit.
